evidence.claim: Buhari said the 2022 budget was the first in Nigeria's history to explicitly advise MDAs on gender-responsive budgeting and described it as a step toward fairer resource distribution and support for vulnerable groups.
evidence.title: 2022 BUDGET SPEECH: (Budget of Economic Growth and Sustainability) Delivered by President Muhammadu Buhari at the Joint Session of the National Assembly, Abuja
evidence.publisher: Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the 2022 budget was the first in Nigeria's history to explicitly advise MDAs on gender-responsive budgeting and described it as a step toward fairer resource distribution and support for vulnerable groups.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential budget speech; authoritative for stated intent and formal priorities, though self-presenting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari action and intent in a formal budget speech.
contrary_evidence: Rhetorical commitment does not prove implementation
later fiscal results were weak

evidence.claim: Buhari said the 2022 budget was guided by diversification, infrastructure investment, better health and education, poverty reduction, and minimizing regional, economic, and social disparities, and that loans would finance roads, rail, power, water, irrigation, and health projects.
evidence.title: 2022 BUDGET SPEECH: (Budget of Economic Growth and Sustainability) Delivered by President Muhammadu Buhari at the Joint Session of the National Assembly, Abuja
evidence.publisher: Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the 2022 budget was guided by diversification, infrastructure investment, better health and education, poverty reduction, and minimizing regional, economic, and social disparities, and that loans would finance roads, rail, power, water, irrigation, and health projects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct speech with concrete fiscal and investment priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari policy agenda, though spending execution depended on ministries and borrowing conditions.
contrary_evidence: Planned priorities were not fully realized in execution
heavy borrowing remained necessary

evidence.claim: The CBN says the 2022 budget was passed and assented to in April 2022 and was tied to the 2021-2025 National Development Plan goals of diversification, infrastructure, security, education, health, poverty reduction, and reducing disparities.
evidence.title: Fiscal Policy
evidence.excerpt: The CBN says the 2022 budget was passed and assented to in April 2022 and was tied to the 2021-2025 National Development Plan goals of diversification, infrastructure, security, education, health, poverty reduction, and reducing disparities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official fiscal summary, dated later but explicitly describing 2022 budget structure and priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: this is the fiscal framework Buhari approved and his administration executed.
contrary_evidence: Describes formal budget design more than outcomes
does not by itself show effective implementation

evidence.claim: The CBN says 2022 total revenue was below budget, capital expenditure was far below plan, and the deficit was financed largely through domestic borrowing and ways-and-means advances; total public debt rose to N46.25 trillion by end-2022.
evidence.title: Fiscal Policy
evidence.excerpt: The CBN says 2022 total revenue was below budget, capital expenditure was far below plan, and the deficit was financed largely through domestic borrowing and ways-and-means advances; total public debt rose to N46.25 trillion by end-2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official summary with concrete budget-performance numbers and year-end debt data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct on Buhari-era fiscal execution, though the borrowing and debt management were partly mediated by finance and monetary institutions.
contrary_evidence: The page still shows the budget framework existed and capital projects were prioritized on paper

evidence.claim: The IMF said higher oil prices created an opportunity to build fiscal space and FX reserves, but that opportunity was not harnessed; inflation was elevated and fuel subsidies remained a formidable drain on fiscal revenues.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2022 Article IV Mission
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said higher oil prices created an opportunity to build fiscal space and FX reserves, but that opportunity was not harnessed; inflation was elevated and fuel subsidies remained a formidable drain on fiscal revenues.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment with explicit macro-fiscal judgment and 2022 timing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Buhari-era macro policy, though constrained by oil theft, global prices, and inherited weaknesses.
contrary_evidence: Nigeria still had positive growth and some revenue gains
the IMF frames the issue as policy choice under constraint

evidence.claim: The IMF welcomed the steady implementation of the TaxPro Max tax automation system and urged broader tax-administration reforms, including better segmentation, customs modernization, and PAYE administration.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2022 Article IV Mission
evidence.excerpt: The IMF welcomed the steady implementation of the TaxPro Max tax automation system and urged broader tax-administration reforms, including better segmentation, customs modernization, and PAYE administration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct, specific policy assessment by the IMF mission.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Buhari administration's revenue apparatus and fiscal team.
contrary_evidence: The IMF presents this as partial progress rather than a completed reform
larger revenue gaps remained

evidence.claim: The IMF said the CBN had raised the policy rate by a cumulative 400 basis points, but monetary conditions were still accommodative because budget financing through the CBN and directed lending programs continued to expand money supply.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2022 Article IV Mission
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the CBN had raised the policy rate by a cumulative 400 basis points, but monetary conditions were still accommodative because budget financing through the CBN and directed lending programs continued to expand money supply.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific policy and macro-finance assessment with explicit numeric details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Buhari-era monetary governance through the CBN, though operationally executed by the central bank.
contrary_evidence: Rate hikes show some stabilization effort
the IMF still judged the stance insufficient

evidence.claim: The World Bank said petrol, electricity, and FX subsidies were inefficient and regressive, benefited primarily wealthy households, distorted incentives, discouraged investment, and crowded out pro-poor programs.
evidence.title: To Promote Inclusive and Sustainable Development, Nigeria Needs to Fix its Public Finances
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said petrol, electricity, and FX subsidies were inefficient and regressive, benefited primarily wealthy households, distorted incentives, discouraged investment, and crowded out pro-poor programs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank press release summarizing a country-specific public finance review with concrete distributional claims.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fiscal debate and year-end assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Buhari-era policy, especially subsidy and FX management.
contrary_evidence: The government had long defended subsidies as social protection
the source is a policy critique rather than a neutral outcome table

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Nigeria's public spending averaged 12 percent of GDP and revenue about 7 percent of GDP from 2015 to 2021, and argued that fiscal reform, a market-based exchange rate, and trade/tax rationalization would improve the business environment and attract FDI.
evidence.title: To Promote Inclusive and Sustainable Development, Nigeria Needs to Fix its Public Finances
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Nigeria's public spending averaged 12 percent of GDP and revenue about 7 percent of GDP from 2015 to 2021, and argued that fiscal reform, a market-based exchange rate, and trade/tax rationalization would improve the business environment and attract FDI.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific quantitative macro-fiscal comparison from a major multilateral review.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Buhari's policy environment; not all figures are exclusively attributable to him, but the 2022 choices are part of the same regime.
contrary_evidence: Low spending/revenue are partly structural and inherited
the report is prescriptive, not a causal identification

evidence.claim: The World Bank said microdata for welfare and poverty analysis are far less frequent than macro data, introduced new analysis on labor markets, climate shocks, and social protection, and stressed that outcomes differ dramatically across Nigerian states, especially north versus south.
evidence.title: Nigeria Poverty Assessment
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said microdata for welfare and poverty analysis are far less frequent than macro data, introduced new analysis on labor markets, climate shocks, and social protection, and stressed that outcomes differ dramatically across Nigerian states, especially north versus south.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank country assessment with clear distributional framing, though the page is high-level rather than the full report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly context rather than direct Buhari attribution, but it frames distributional constraints his government faced.
contrary_evidence: It describes structural data limitations more than a Buhari choice
state disparities predate 2022

evidence.claim: NBS reported headline inflation of 21.34 percent in December 2022, up 5.72 percentage points year on year from December 2021, with the 12-month average CPI also rising further.
evidence.title: CPI and Inflation Report December 2022
evidence.excerpt: NBS reported headline inflation of 21.34 percent in December 2022, up 5.72 percentage points year on year from December 2021, with the 12-month average CPI also rising further.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National statistical release with clear numeric time series.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome under Buhari's 2022 macroeconomic management, though influenced by global food and fuel shocks.
contrary_evidence: Inflation eased slightly month to month in December
some of the pressure was externally driven

evidence.claim: NBS reported that 36.4 percent of employed persons worked fewer than 40 hours per week in Q4 2022, underemployment was 13.7 percent, and short-hours work was most common among women, younger people, those with less education, and rural residents.
evidence.title: Nigeria Labour Force Survey Q4 2022 & Q1 2023
evidence.excerpt: NBS reported that 36.4 percent of employed persons worked fewer than 40 hours per week in Q4 2022, underemployment was 13.7 percent, and short-hours work was most common among women, younger people, those with less education, and rural residents.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official labor-force release with a clear household/employment distribution pattern.
evidence.period_fit: Directly overlaps Q4 2022 and is close to the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual to Buhari-era labor conditions, not a single ruler action, but relevant to distributional performance.
contrary_evidence: Headline employment rates were still fairly high
the report measures hours/underemployment rather than earnings or poverty directly

evidence.claim: The World Bank said development had stagnated over the last decade, private investment was declining, and Nigeria needed macro stability, exchange-rate reform, lower trade barriers, higher non-oil revenues, and fixes to power, finance, and digitalization constraints.
evidence.title: Nigeria Country Economic Memorandum: Charting a New Course
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said development had stagnated over the last decade, private investment was declining, and Nigeria needed macro stability, exchange-rate reform, lower trade barriers, higher non-oil revenues, and fixes to power, finance, and digitalization constraints.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank diagnosis with concrete growth and investment constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly regime-level and structural, but highly relevant to Buhari's final-year economic stewardship.
contrary_evidence: The memo covers the prior decade, not only 2022
it identifies structural and inherited constraints

evidence.claim: Buhari assigned portfolios to seven newly appointed ministers, said the redeployment was meant to reinvigorate sectors where better results were desired, and told the new team to serve diligently and focus on key programs.
evidence.title: Serve the Nation Diligently, President Buhari Charges Newly Appointed Ministers; Re-assigns Four Others
evidence.excerpt: Buhari assigned portfolios to seven newly appointed ministers, said the redeployment was meant to reinvigorate sectors where better results were desired, and told the new team to serve diligently and focus on key programs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential announcement of cabinet changes and purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari cabinet choice and administrative direction.
contrary_evidence: The speech is generic and does not prove competence
the reshuffle is not itself evidence of outcomes

evidence.claim: Buhari said ministers and political appointees seeking elective office should resign their current appointments, said replacements would be made without delay, and described the cabinet departure as a normal transition.
evidence.title: President Buhari to Outgoing Ministers: Significant Number of You Sufficiently Equipped to Be My Successor
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said ministers and political appointees seeking elective office should resign their current appointments, said replacements would be made without delay, and described the cabinet departure as a normal transition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential directive and cabinet-management statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari action on appointments and entrenchment risk.
contrary_evidence: Several ministers were themselves seeking office, so the cabinet was not apolitical
this does not resolve broader CBN politicization

evidence.claim: ICIR said Emefiele's 2022 presidential ambition became a major controversy, that he announced it after meeting Buhari, and that Finance Minister Zainab Ahmed said she had not been informed about the naira-redesign plan.
evidence.title: Godwin Emefiele: CBN governor in the eye of the storm
evidence.excerpt: ICIR said Emefiele's 2022 presidential ambition became a major controversy, that he announced it after meeting Buhari, and that Finance Minister Zainab Ahmed said she had not been informed about the naira-redesign plan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Investigative local reporting with concrete contemporaneous details and named participants.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but materially attributable to Buhari's administration because the CBN governor operated under his tenure and met with him before the announcement.
contrary_evidence: The piece is retrospective and investigative rather than a formal inquiry
it reflects controversy and capture risk more than a full causal finding

evidence.claim: Buhari said the redesigned naira would help address illicit financial flows, corruption, the economy, and the value of the currency, while the CBN said the policy would help control money supply and support monetary policy.
evidence.title: Buhari unveils redesigned naira notes
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the redesigned naira would help address illicit financial flows, corruption, the economy, and the value of the currency, while the CBN said the policy would help control money supply and support monetary policy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a formal policy unveiling with direct quotes from Buhari and Emefiele.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari and CBN policy intent.
contrary_evidence: The policy later triggered cash-scarcity problems
intent to fight corruption does not prove effective implementation

evidence.claim: Reuters said the redesigned naira notes were in short supply on the first day of circulation, while many Nigerians said the deadline was too tight, especially for rural and informal-market users.
evidence.title: New Nigerian naira notes a rare sight on first day of circulation
evidence.excerpt: Reuters said the redesigned naira notes were in short supply on the first day of circulation, while many Nigerians said the deadline was too tight, especially for rural and informal-market users.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with clear contemporaneous market and household impact, albeit via a republication page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly linked to Buhari's approved policy, though the operational failure was executed by the CBN.
contrary_evidence: This is launch-day evidence, not a full medium-run evaluation
the policy aim was anti-corruption and cash control

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice under Buhari's own authority
Independent corroboration of the HEU-to-LEU conversion and other nuclear-security claims
Independent evidence of actual conflict-management effect from Buhari's Ukraine/ECOWAS diplomacy
Direct documentary support for the contested Lake Chad weapons claim or any concrete cross-border security outcome
More precise chain-of-command and federal-versus-state attribution for abuses and remedies
More direct evidence on Buhari's personal role in media and protest restrictions, beyond security-service and state-level actions
Independent implementation evidence for the 2022 Electoral Act and related reforms
More household-level and distributional evidence on the effects of subsidy, naira redesign, and fiscal choices
Cleaner evidence on whether economic appointees were selected for competence versus loyalty
Independent outcome evaluation of school feeding, BHCPF, rotavirus rollout, and related social programs
Subnational delivery and attribution, especially for north-south and rural-urban differences
Direct evidence on assets, beneficial ownership, gifts, campaign finance, or family enrichment
More independent evidence on truthfulness, correction, and acceptance of scrutiny
Better separation of Buhari's personal conduct from broader authoritarian or state-level behavior
Audited completion data for major projects and service-delivery claims
Independent evidence that coordination bodies and new appointments changed implementation quality
